title: Recognition of a finite normal model of an integral blowup
statement:
Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], $J\subset\mathcal O_X$ a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and $p:B=\operatorname{Bl}_JX	o X$ its ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $U\subset X$ be a nonempty dense open with $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Let $f:Y	o B$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], where $Y$ is a locally Noetherian scheme all of whose local rings are normal domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose $V=(p\circ f)^{-1}U$ is dense in $Y$ and $V	o U$ is an isomorphism. Then $B$ and $Y$ are integral, $f$ is surjective, and their function fields identify canonically with $k(X)$ [def-sc-function-field]. For every nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset B$, write $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}C)=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Via the common function field, $C\subset D\subset k(X)$, and $D$ equals the integral closure of $C$ in $k(X)$. These affine identifications give the unique $B$-isomorphism $Y\simeq B^
u$ with $f=
u\circ(Y\simeq B^
u)$, where $
u:B^
u	o B$ is normalization in the function field [def-sc-normalization]. No excellence assumption or prior finiteness assumption on $
u$ is required.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, normalization part; finite normal-model recognition expanded in the returned proof, steps 7--8. Stacks 02ND (divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme) for integrality of the ordinary blowup; integral closure is as in def-sc-normalization.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry], $B$ is integral: its hypotheses are precisely integrality of $X$ and nonzero finite-type quasi-coherence of $J$. Put $W=p^{-1}U$. Since $J|_U=\mathcal O_U$, $U$ is contained in $X\setminus V(J)$, and [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] restricts to an isomorphism $W\simeq U$. Thus $W$ is nonempty and open in the integral scheme $B$, hence dense. The given isomorphism $V\simeq U$ identifies $f|_V:V\to W$ with an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02ND, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme; Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor, isomorphism off the center

proof.text: The nonempty open $U$ of the integral scheme $X$ is irreducible, so its isomorphic copy $V$ is irreducible. Since $\overline V=Y$, $Y$ is irreducible: if $Y=F_1\cup F_2$ with $F_i$ closed, irreducibility gives $V\subset F_i$ for one $i$, and closure gives $Y=F_i$. Every local ring of $Y$ is a domain, hence reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme] this makes $Y$ reduced; it is nonempty because $V$ is. The reduced-and-irreducible characterization in [def-pc-integral-scheme] now makes $Y$ integral.

The finite morphism $f$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Its image contains $W$, so the density of $W$ gives $f(Y)=B$, so $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The generic point of any integral scheme lies in every nonempty open, and its stalk is unchanged on restriction to that open [def-sc-function-field, lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Thus $p|_W:W\simeq U$ and $f|_V:V\simeq W$ identify the respective generic stalks as $k(B)\simeq k(U)\simeq k(X)$ and $k(Y)\simeq k(B)$. These are the identifications induced by $p$ and $f$, since all the maps on the common open are their restrictions.

source.place: Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper; Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; Tag 01RW, definition-function-field

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normal-cover-normalization] to $f:Y	o B$. Its hypotheses hold: $B$ and $Y$ are integral by steps 1--2; $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] by assumption; $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective by step 3; and the induced map $F=k(B)	o L=k(Y)$ is the isomorphism of step 3, so $L/F$ is finite (of degree $1$). For a nonempty affine $A=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset B$ with $f^{-1}A=\operatorname{Spec}D$, the cited statement gives that $C	o D$ is injective and that, under the germ embedding $D\subseteq L=\operatorname{Frac}D$, $D$ is the integral closure of $C$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Transporting along the identifications $L\simeq k(B)\simeq k(X)$ of step 3 gives $C\subset D\subset K=k(X)$ with $D=\overline C$, the integral closure of $C$ in $K$. The cited statement also gives a canonical $B$-isomorphism $e:Y\simeq B^L$, where $B^L$ is the normalization of $B$ in $L$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Since $F	o L$ is an isomorphism, the integral closure of $\mathcal O_B$ in the constant sheaf $L$ is the image of its integral closure in $F=k(B)$, so $B^L$ is $B^F$, which is exactly $B^
u$ of [def-sc-normalization] by the case $L=K$ of [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Thus $e$ gives $\alpha:Y\simeq B^
u$ over $B$, i.e. $f=
u\circ\alpha$, and over $A$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the identification $\overline C=D$ inside $K$.

source.place: Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization; Tag 035I, normalization in a finite extension (via lem-sfb-finite-normal-cover-normalization); algebra.tex Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral

proof.text:
For uniqueness let $ eta:Y	o B^
u$ be any $B$-morphism (in particular any competing $B$-isomorphism). Over a nonempty affine $A=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset B$, $ eta$ maps $f^{-1}A=\operatorname{Spec}D$ into $
u^{-1}A=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ (step 4 and the affine description in [def-fin-normalization-extension]), so it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a $C$-algebra map $h:\overline C	o D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; let $\alpha^\sharp:\overline C	o D$ be the identification of step 4. For $z\in\overline C\subset K=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] choose $a,b\in C$, $b
e0$, with $bz=a$. Then $b\,h(z)=a=b\,\alpha^\sharp(z)$ in the domain $D$, and $b
eq0$ in $D$ since $C	o D$ is injective, so $h(z)=\alpha^\sharp(z)$. Thus $ eta=\alpha$ on every $f^{-1}A$, and globally by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Each $\overline C=D$ is finite over $C$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so $
u$ is finite as a consequence of the given finite $f$, not by assumption; excellence was nowhere used.

source.place: Tag 00GP, definition-integral-closure; uniqueness by fraction-field denominators; schemes.tex Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes
